sentences: Nearly 2,000 years ago, as the Romans began to pull out of Scotland, they left behind a curious treasure: 10 tons of nails, nearly a million of the things.
The nail hoard was discovered in 1960 in a four-metre-deep pit covered by two metres of gravel.
translations: 大约2000年前，当罗马人开始撤离苏格兰时，他们留下了一笔奇怪的财富：10吨钉子，将近一百万枚。
这批钉子是在1960年被发现的，埋在一个四米深、上面覆盖着两米砾石的坑里。

sentences: Why had the Romans buried a million nails?
The likely explanation is that the withdrawal was rushed, and they didn’t want the local Caledonians getting their hands on 10 tons of weapon-grade iron.
The Romans buried the nails so deep that they would not be discovered for almost two millennia.
translations: 为什么罗马人要埋藏一百万枚钉子呢？
可能的解释是，撤离很匆忙，他们不想让当地的加勒多尼亚人得到10吨武器级的铁。
罗马人把钉子埋得如此之深，以至于它们几乎两千年都未被发现。

sentences: Later civilisations would value the skilled blacksmith’s labour in a nail even more than the raw material.
As Roma Agrawal explains in her new delightful book Nuts and Bolts, early 17th-century Virginians would sometimes burn down their homes if they were planning to relocate.
This was an attempt to recover the valuable nails, which could be reused after sifting the ashes.
The idea that one might burn down an entire house just to reclaim the nails underlines how scarce, costly and valuable the simple-seeming technology was.
translations: 后来的文明对钉子中熟练铁匠劳动的重视程度甚至超过了原材料本身。
正如罗马·阿格拉瓦尔在她那本令人愉快的新书《螺母与螺栓》中所解释的，17世纪初的弗吉尼亚人有时会在计划搬迁时烧毁自己的房屋。
这是为了回收那些宝贵的钉子，这些钉子可以在筛过灰烬后重新使用。
为了回收钉子而烧毁整栋房子的想法，突显了这种看似简单的技术是多么稀缺、昂贵和珍贵。

sentences: The price of nails fell by 90% between the late 1700s and mid-1900s, as economist Daniel Sichel points out in a research paper.

According to Sichel, although the falling price of nails was driven partly by cheaper iron and cheaper energy, most of the credit goes to nail manufacturers who simply found more efficient ways to turn steel into nails.
translations: 正如经济学家丹尼尔·西歇尔在一篇研究论文中指出的，从18世纪末到20世纪中叶，钉子的价格下降了90%。
根据西歇尔的说法，尽管钉子价格下跌部分是由更便宜的铁和更便宜的能源推动的，但主要功劳应归于那些找到了更有效方法将钢转化为钉子的钉子制造商。

sentences: Nails themselves have changed over the years, but Sichel studied them because they haven’t changed much.
Roman lamps and Roman chariots are very different from LED strips and sports cars, but Roman nails are still clearly nails.
It would be absurd to try to track the changing price of sports cars since 1695, but to ask the same question of nails makes perfect sense.
translations: 钉子本身多年来有所变化，但西歇尔研究它们是因为它们变化不大。
罗马的灯和罗马的战车与LED灯条和跑车大不相同，但罗马的钉子显然还是钉子。
试图追踪自1695年以来跑车价格的变化是荒谬的，但对钉子提出同样的问题则完全合理。

sentences: I make no apology for being obsessed by a particular feature of everyday objects: their price.
I am an economist, after all.

After writing two books about the history of inventions, one thing I’ve learnt is that while it is the enchantingly sophisticated technologies that get all the hype, it’s the cheap technologies that change the world.
translations: 我毫不抱歉地痴迷于日常物品的一个特定特征：它们的价格。
毕竟，我是一名经济学家。
在写了两本关于发明史的书之后，我学到的一件事是，虽然那些迷人复杂的技术获得了所有炒作，但改变世界的是廉价技术。

sentences: The Gutenberg printing press transformed civilisation not by changing the nature of writing but by changing its cost—and it would have achieved little without a parallel collapse in the price of surfaces to write on, thanks to an often-overlooked technology called paper.
Solar panels had a few niche uses until they became cheap; now they are transforming the global energy system.
translations: 古腾堡印刷机改变文明不是通过改变写作的性质，而是通过改变其成本——如果没有一种经常被忽视的叫做纸的技术使得书写表面价格同步暴跌，它几乎不会取得什么成就。
太阳能电池板在变得便宜之前只有一些利基用途；现在它们正在改变全球能源系统。

sentences:
21. The Romans buried the nails probably for the sake of
A. saving them for future use
B. keeping them from rusting
C. letting them grow in value
D. hiding them from the locals
translations:
21. 罗马人埋藏钉子可能是为了
A. 把它们留作将来使用
B. 防止它们生锈
C. 让它们增值
D. 不让当地人发现它们

sentences:
22. The example of early 17th-century Virginians is used to
A. highlight the thriftiness of early American colonists
B. illustrate the high status of blacksmiths in that period
C. contrast the attitudes of different civilisations towards nails
D. show the preciousness of nail-making technology at that time
translations:
22. 早期17世纪弗吉尼亚人的例子被用来
A. 强调早期美国殖民者的节俭
B. 说明那个时期铁匠的高地位
C. 对比不同文明对钉子的态度
D. 展示当时制钉技术的珍贵性

sentences:
23. What played the major role in lowering the price of nails after the late 1700s?
A. Increased Productivity.
B. Wider use of new energies.
C. Fiercer market competition.
D. Reduced cost of raw materials.
translations:
23. 在18世纪末之后，什么在降低钉子价格方面起了主要作用？
A. 生产力的提高。
B. 新能源的更广泛使用。
C. 更激烈的市场竞争。
D. 原材料成本的降低。

sentences:
24. It can be learned from Paragraph 5 that nails
A. have undergone many technological improvements
B. have remained basically the same since Roman times
C. are less studied than other everyday products
D. are one of the world’s most significant inventions
translations:
24. 从第五段可以了解到，钉子
A. 经历了许多技术改进
B. 自罗马时代以来基本保持不变
C. 比其他日常产品研究得少
D. 是世界上最重要的发明之一

sentences:
25. Which of the following best summarises the last two paragraphs?
A. Cheap technologies bring about revolutionary change.
B. Technological innovation is integral to economic success.
C. Technology defines people’s understanding of the world.
D. Sophisticated technologies develop from small inventions.
translations:
25. 以下哪项最能概括最后两段？
A. 廉价技术带来革命性的变化。
B. 技术创新是经济成功不可或缺的一部分。
C. 技术定义了人们对世界的理解。
D. 复杂技术是从小发明发展而来的。
